_comment: Checked in on purpose: these grants ARE the project's shipping policy and should
travel with the repo, not live in one machine's settings.local.json. The matching
prose is CLAUDE.md section 'Shipping - what a session may do without asking'.
Codex reads none of this. Its copy of the same policy is .codex/rules/shipping.rules,
and the two must be changed together - see CLAUDE.md section 'Your agent'.
Push rules are SCOPED, never a blanket Bash(git push:*).
LIMIT, not papered over: Bash rules are PREFIX matches, so the deny list below
cannot catch a --force placed at the END of a command. Forbidding force-push is
prose in CLAUDE.md; this file cannot enforce it.
scripts/release.sh is the only route to main: a direct 'git push origin main' is
DENIED so the script's preconditions (clean tree, unused tag, main not ahead of
develop) cannot be walked around. A session must pass --yes; the retype prompt
reads stdin, which is closed non-interactively.
CHANGEME: the docker --context line in the allow list is the manual production
deploy. It is the one entry to review per project - delete it on a project that
deploys only through deploy/ or the self-hosted runner.
